details_checked: Candidate header, scope `direct`, version `v0`, and SHA-256 digest match the registered review target.

All eleven canonical-brief acceptance criteria are addressed with concrete navigation, page-anatomy, route-specific, responsive, state, implementation, verification, rollback, option-ledger, and research-unknown detail.

The candidate explicitly covers Dashboard, Ticket Queue, Ticket Detail, Services, Problems, Changes, Assets, Knowledge Base, Agents, Surveys, Leaderboard, My Time, Reports, Intelligence, and Settings.

Compatibility and adversarial state checks preserve current access checks, demo restrictions, API/query contracts, safe external URLs, mutations, independent failure paths, loading, empty, filtered-empty, partial/stale, unauthorized, and destructive-confirmation behavior.
Responsive arrangements, keyboard operation, focus containment/restoration, semantic state, accessible alternatives, and rollback/stop boundaries are specific and testable.
implementation_options: N1 — Rejected: a flat reorder does not resolve scanning cost.
N2 — Selected: visible domain groups retain direct destination access and existing gates.
N3 — Deferred: collapsible groups would hide destinations and add focus/state complexity.
N4 — Rejected: personalization lacks usage evidence and makes placement unstable.
P1 — Rejected: tokens alone leave hierarchy and duplication unresolved.
P2 plus page families — Selected: canonical anatomy allows justified route-specific exceptions.
P3 — Rejected: a rigid KPI/template system produces decorative repetition.
D1 — Rejected: showing all controls overweights secondary metadata.
D2 — Rejected: aggressive hiding harms discovery and expert speed.
D3 — Selected: progressive disclosure keeps common work visible.
T1 — Rejected: a vertical ticket stack preserves equal weighting and long travel.
T2 — Selected at xl: activity plus a properties rail preserves essential context.
T3 — Rejected: a fully tabbed record page fragments essential context.
R1 — Rejected: one app-wide rewrite has excessive regression and rollback risk.
R2 — Rejected: independent cosmetic edits would recreate drift.
R3 — Selected: shared primitives followed by critical-route migration is reversible and testable.
